reviews.rationale: Nonstops are selected when they protect setup, sleep, or a next-day teaching obligation, but connections are repeatedly booked when their timing and cost remain workable. The record supports trip-specific schedule-risk comparison, not a categorical routing preference.

Later departures are often imposed by current classes, calls, or webinars. Early morning departures are also accepted when they are needed for setup, presenter check-in, or reliable arrival, so there is no reusable late-departure preference.

Changed flights are kept when the revised timing still preserves the trip's commitments, and switched when they create a risky connection, undermine setup, or materially worsen recovery. No fixed keep-or-switch response is supported.

Extra nights are added when teardown, equipment, traffic, or late arrivals make same-day travel brittle, but same-day returns are booked when a firm release time makes them comfortably workable. Return-day choice is event- and schedule-dependent.

Cars are used when they solve regional driving, early starts, gear, parking, or loading logistics. They are avoided when onsite storage, urban parking, short distances, or rideshare simplicity make them unnecessary. Neither rentals nor rideshare are a fixed default.

Suites are often chosen when confirmed bed, fridge, coffee, workspace, and recovery features outweigh commute cost. Official or connected hotels are chosen when conference proximity and material movement outweigh the room-certainty advantage. Hotel format remains conditional.

Farther or alternate airports win only when flight timing, fare, rental availability, or return-day options offset added driving. Closer or primary airports win when they reduce ground risk or avoid unnecessary crosstown travel. There is no portable alternate-airport default.

The record supports requesting windows when included, but fee decisions vary by price, segment importance, adjacency, and current trip cost. Kara sometimes approves modest fees and sometimes declines comparable or higher fees, so willingness to pay is not a stable default.
